Hi Jordan / Alex — thanks for the details and the diagram. Quick answers and recommended next steps below.

1) Support: PrivateLink + VPC Peering
- Redwood Private supports both AWS PrivateLink and VPC Peering. For our hosted Private offering: 
  - PrivateLink: recommended when customers require strict private connectivity without routing table changes on the Redwood side; generally preferred for minimal blast radius and simpler customer-side firewall rules.
  - VPC Peering: recommended when you want direct VPC-to-VPC connectivity and slightly lower latency at high throughput. Peering requires route table updates and cross-account routing.

2) Tradeoffs for your workload (~120 QPS, 120-token avg):
- Latency: Peering can be ~10-30ms lower median latency at very high sustained throughput, but for your target p50 (200-300ms) both options are viable.
- Ops: PrivateLink typically simplifies customer firewall rules (you only need to allow outbound to the endpoint) and is easier for security teams to reason about; peering requires route adjustments and potential overlap checks for CIDRs.

3) IP allowlisting & stable ranges
- For PrivateLink, customers typically allow the PrivateLink VPC endpoint DNS and security group; no public IP allowlist required.
- For VPC Peering or if you need egress through our NAT, we can provide stable egress IPs per environment. Provisional ranges (please treat as placeholders until legal/ops sign-off):
  - staging (us-west-2): 54.173.100.20
  - prod (us-west-2): 54.173.101.45
  - prod (us-east-1): 3.12.45.88
- If your security policy requires contiguous CIDRs only, we can provide a /24 on request after we reserve capacity; otherwise allowlisting per-IP is OK.

4) Info we need from you to proceed:
- AWS account ID(s) for the VPC(s) you want connected
- VPC ID(s) + primary CIDR(s)
- Preferred option: PrivateLink or Peering (or undecided)
- Any IP ranges or firewall rules restrictions on your side (eg only outbound to specific /32s)
- A point-of-contact for tunnel/testing windows (SRE/network engineer)

5) Proposed next steps & timeline
- You (Acme) provide details listed above by EOD 4/3.
- Redwood infra (me + Marissa) will produce a short network design doc and final egress IPs within 48 hours of receiving VPC/account info.
- Schedule a 30-min network handshake call to validate firewall rules and test traffic (we can do this next week).

Attachment: redwood_network_requirements.pdf (detailed requirements + checklist).

If helpful I can also put together a 1-page tradeoff doc that Marissa can send to your security team summarizing PrivateLink vs Peering. Happy to jump on a quick call — propose Tue/Wed next week for the network handshake.

Thanks,
